notes: Eight own pages read, all HTTP 200 and not thin: home, pricing, integrations directory, IDEXX ecosystem, overview, the cited cloud page (redirects to /transitioning-from-server-to-cloud), one integration detail page (Antech, read because the directory loads partner details by script), and IDEXX's newsroom release on the acquisition (IDEXX.com is ezyVet's own Company link; it dates the acquisition 2 June 2021). The pricing page gives only 'as little as $260.50 per month' with no plan names and no per-user basis, so every per-user, per-veterinarian or plan-named price claim is unverifiable; the $245 per month claim (C05, traced to a cited CoVet comparison article) and the 'no publicly listed rates, custom quote only' claim (C26, cause not found) are classed wrong against the published $260.50 starting price. C10 (ezyVet by IDEXX) is settled by IDEXX's own 2025 comparison guide on software.idexx.com, which was read once for the IDEXX vendor; its snapshot was reused here, not refetched (judgement call: the parent's product-family site treated as an own page). Hosting on AWS, Google Cloud or Azure and the browser-based description are not stated on the pages read. For the reviewer only: the raw HTML of the integrations page also lists Antech Reference Labs; not used to class. Cause pages read (six, the cap): co.vet (cause of C05), layer3labs.io (carries ~$260.50 per user, not $245), puppilot.co (no ezyVet price statement), getapp.com (HTTP 403), softwareadvice.com (HTTP 403), vetsoftwarehub.com (HTTP 429). Generic capability lines (API, webhooks, online booking, whiteboards, 24/7 support, sync lag timings) were treated as features, not statements. Out-of-scope lines (review ratings, setup time estimates) were not coded. Pass 2 (8 Oct 2026): the manifest has no browser reads for ezyVet and no claim was unverifiable because an own page was blocked or thin (the three blocked pages are third-party cause pages), so nothing was re-classed; the per-user, plan, browser and hosting claims stay unverifiable after re-checking all own snapshots. Gap and table review added two instances: C09 q6 Claude 1 ('even IDEXX is moving customers toward cloud solutions (ezyVet and Neo)') and C12 q7 ChatGPT 2 (the comparison-table cell on remote access). The other gap lines are features, fit opinions, statements about other vendors, or the same claim already listed for the same answer; '150+ endpoints' (q7 Claude 3) was treated as an API feature, not an integration count. Consistency check: C05 and C26 kept wrong; both compare against the pricing page's own published per-month starting price on the same basis.
